title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter II of a 1986 manuscript on topological realizations of 'réseaux'. A 'ficelle' (string) appears to be a compact triangulated space X with a pair {A,B} of disjoint, nonempty closed subsets (probably subcomplexes) called the ends. An 'oriented' ficelle has an ordered pair (A source, B target). The previous page studied the 'lieux' (separating loci) of a ficelle, which form a dense bounded ordered set, and cutting X along n disjoint loci, which amounts to gluing n+1 ficelles. This page asks which constraints should be put on such data.

(1) Existence. A compact triangulated X admits a ficelle structure iff X is connected and not a point. Take two distinct vertices, or two disjoint subcomplexes. Grothendieck comments 'C'est gros!', meaning the notion as it stands is far too permissive. A struck passage makes the same point. If (X,{A,B}) is a ficelle and A', B' are disjoint closed neighbourhoods with A⊂A' and B⊂B', then (X,{A',B'}) is again a ficelle. So the only real condition is that the ends are disjoint closed sets in a connected X.

(2) Segment. A margin note says that on [0,1] the ficelle structures are, up to homeomorphism, {[0,α],[β,1]} with 0≤α<β≤1.

(3) Equivalence. Consider the equivalence relation on ficelle structures (resp. oriented ones) generated by enlargement: A⊂A' and B⊂B'. A first claim, 'Inversement…', is struck and replaced by 'Two oriented ficelle structures on a triangulated X are always equivalent.' The margin then corrects this: 'Faux — idem!' and 'Faux déjà (en orienté!) dans le cas des segments!'.

Modern reading: shrink each end to a point inside it. The question then becomes whether any two ordered pairs of distinct points are joined in the ordered configuration space F(X,2). For an interval, (0,1) and (1,0) are not joined. This matches the elementary fact that, for a connected finite complex X, F(X,2) is connected iff X is not homeomorphic to an arc. Graphs with a branch point allow the 'Y-swap'; dimension ≥2 or a circle allow passing around. In the unoriented case, all structures on a connected X (not a point) are equivalent.

Purpose: having seen that bare ficelles are trivial up to this equivalence, he prepares, on the next page, to impose conditions on A, B and the loci. These include connectedness, contractibility, being homeomorphic to a fixed space P, and conditions on boundaries of tubular neighbourhoods. The aim is to get meaningful 'topological realizations' of networks/ordered diagrams.
errors: The main-text claim that any two oriented ficelle structures on a triangulated X are equivalent is false for X a segment: the two orientations cannot be connected. Grothendieck catches this himself in the margin.

The bracket 'Si X est un segment, cette str. est unique. C'est le seul cas d'unicité' is ambiguous and sits uneasily with the margin note, which lists a one-parameter family [0,α], [β,1]. It is presumably meant 'up to equivalence/homeomorphism'. The precise intended statement is unclear.
The exact definition of the generated relation is left loose: the first attempt is struck, and the role of the '(resp. orientée)' variant is not specified.

ideas.what: Criterion: a compact triangulated space carries a two-ended 'string' structure iff it is connected and not a point; the notion is too coarse ('C'est gros!').
ideas.modern_name: bipointed / two-ended spaces, cospans of subspaces

ideas.what: Equivalence of string structures generated by enlarging the ends; in the oriented case it fails only for the segment.
ideas.modern_name: connectedness of the ordered configuration space F(X,2) (fails exactly for the arc among connected finite complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; graph configuration spaces studied by Abrams, Ghrist and others in the 1990s–2000s

ideas.what: Classification of string structures on [0,1] up to homeomorphism as {[0,α],[β,1]}.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working note recording that the naive notion of 'ficelle' is trivial up to the natural equivalence. Grothendieck then corrects his own overclaim (orientation matters for segments). The mathematics is elementary and serves only to motivate the restrictions on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Title: possibly 'Conditions particulières sur les lieux' (consistent with the previous page's 'lieux') rather than 'liens'; the handwriting is ambiguous.
'Il y a alors ∞ une structure de ficelle réduite' — the image more plausibly reads 'Il y a alors une structure de ficelle évidente' (uncertain); '∞' is doubtful.
'où B est la relation d'ordre' — the symbol is likely '≤' or 'à', not ℬ; read '... la relation d'équivalence (resp. orientée) engendrée par A⊂A' et B⊂B''.
Bottom margin includes '(Conorientée!)' / '(en orienté!)' next to 'Faux déjà dans le cas des segments!'.
Margin 'à homéo près' is uncertain; it could be 'à isom. près'.
